text: The men of Ephraim were mustered, and they crossed over to Zaphon and said to Jephthah, "Why did you cross over to fight the Ammonites without calling us to go with you? We will burn your house down over your head!"

versions.text: The men of Ephraim were called out, and they crossed over to Zaphon and said to Jephthah, "Why did you cross over to fight the Ammonites without calling us to go with you? We will burn your house down over your head!"
versions.explanation: "Were called out" is vague for the niphal of צעק (to be summoned to arms); "were mustered" reads more clearly aloud. Also consider a footnote on צָפוֹנָה, which may be read either as the place name Zaphon or as the direction "northward."

text: Jephthah answered them, "I and my people were locked in a bitter struggle with the Ammonites. I called you, but you did not rescue me from their hand.

When I saw that you would not save me, I took my life in my own hands and crossed over against the Ammonites, and the LORD gave them into my hand. So why have you come up against me today to fight me?"

Then Jephthah gathered all the men of Gilead and fought Ephraim, and the men of Gilead struck Ephraim down, because they had said, "You Gileadites are nothing but fugitives from Ephraim, living in the midst of Ephraim and Manasseh."

The Gileadites seized the fords of the Jordan against Ephraim, and whenever an Ephraimite fugitive said, "Let me cross over," the men of Gilead would ask him, "Are you an Ephraimite?" If he said, "No,"

they would say to him, "Then say 'Shibboleth.'" And he would say, "Sibboleth," for he could not pronounce it correctly. Then they would seize him and kill him at the fords of the Jordan. Forty-two thousand of Ephraim fell at that time.
Jephthah judged Israel six years. Then Jephthah the Gileadite died and was buried in one of the towns of Gilead.

versions.text: Jephthah judged Israel six years. Then Jephthah the Gileadite died and was buried in his town in Gilead.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew reads "in the cities of Gilead" (בְּעָרֵי גִלְעָד). "His town" reflects a different textual tradition and introduces information not in the Hebrew; "one of the towns of Gilead" renders the Hebrew idiom naturally without adding a possessive.

text: After him Ibzan of Bethlehem judged Israel.
He had thirty sons, and thirty daughters whom he gave in marriage, and he brought in thirty daughters for his sons from elsewhere. He judged Israel seven years.
Then Ibzan died and was buried in Bethlehem.
After him Elon the Zebulunite judged Israel, and he judged Israel ten years.
Then Elon the Zebulunite died and was buried at Aijalon in the land of Zebulun.
After him Abdon son of Hillel, from Pirathon, judged Israel.
He had forty sons and thirty grandsons, who rode on seventy donkeys. He judged Israel eight years.
Then Abdon son of Hillel, from Pirathon, died and was buried at Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, in the hill country of the Amalekites.
